title: 0936-weighted-hybrid-behavioral-ratings
universal_lens: Weighted hybrid behavioral ratings unify single-factor metrics via latent variable decomposition and outcome-driven weighting, bridging 0934 sum-aggregation and 0936 max-aggregation through game-theoretic optimization. \Omega(p) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i \cdot f_i(\mathbf{x}) \text{ unifies Skill, Support, Strategy via logistic-weighted factor analysis}
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over Ω_QB(p) to generate uncertainty-aware player ratings, enabling Bayesian decision-making under epistemic risk. Bayesian belief updates on \Omega(p) using conformal prediction for ATS outlier detection with Harm asymmetry thresholds
gse_mapping: GSE models team dynamics using max-vs-sum aggregation operators on Ω_QB(p) and position-level Ω, enabling state transitions between tactical configurations during gameplay. Situational state transitions in \Omega(p) space guide real-time player/team rating adjustments under self-destruction risk dynamics

primitives.name: Z-Score Standardization
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Assumptions: Z-scored features comparable; higher hybrid rating → higher win chance; max-member team aggregation; oblique rotation allows correlated factors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'z_i': 'dimensionless standardized score', 'x_i': 'original feature value', '\\mu_x': 'mean of feature distribution', '\\sigma_x': 'standard deviation of feature distribution'}
primitives.assumptions: Equal variance across features after standardization; linear relationships preserved; comparable scale for additive hybrid models.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when input features have heterogeneous variances without transformation, causing weighting bias.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic skill estimation via Gaussian process latent variables, where empirical moments are matched to prior distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation mean squared error on holdout test sets.

primitives.name: Max-Member Team Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Features / target Inputs: per-player cumulative behavioral features → factors → single/hybrid ratings.
primitives.assumptions: Team performance dominated by strongest member; independent identically distributed player skills; no synergy effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when team composition has complementary skillsets, leading to overestimation of team strength.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's multi-agent reinforcement learning where the highest Q-value agent leads negotiation, assuming dominant strategy.
layer2.telemetry: Win-rate differential between predicted max-rating team and opponent teams.

primitives.name: Oblique Factor Rotation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Target: match outcome (head-to-head: accuracy) or rank list (battle royale: NDCG).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'factor loading matrix', 'B': 'oblique rotation matrix', 'Q': 'orthogonal factor scores'}
primitives.assumptions: Correlated underlying skill dimensions; linear mixture model holds; variance explained by each factor is additive but not mutually exclusive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when factors become perfectly collinear, rendering the rotation matrix singular.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's dynamic factor analysis with time-varying loadings, where contemporaneous correlations are modeled as covariance matrices.
layer2.telemetry: Explained variance ratio from principal components analysis.

primitives.name: Weighted Hybrid Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Weighted hybrid Ω is best overall in all 12 cells.** Naive hybrid η also beats systems in most cells (e.g., PUBG top-tier 70.1 vs Elo 71.7 — one of few misses).
primitives.latex: \Omega = w_1 F_1 + w_2 F_2 + ... + w_n F_n
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Omega': 'weighted hybrid rating', 'w_i': 'weight assigned to factor i', 'F_i': 'normalized factor score'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear superposition of factors; optimal weights maximize predictive accuracy; cross-validation prevents overfitting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses when weights become negative or exceed unity, violating non-negativity constraints.

layer2.mapping: Derives from GSE's state-action value function decomposition into policy and value components, where weights are learned from historical transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error reduction relative to baseline systems.

primitives.name: Weighted Hybrid Behavioral Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: Z-score, factor-analyze (expect Skill/Support/Strategy/Experience factors), weight factors by logistic regression on game outcomes 2018–2021, build Ω_QB(p) = Σω̂·factor.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Omega_{\\text{QB}}(p)': 'dimensionless composite player rating', '\\hat{\\omega}_i': 'learned weight coefficient for feature i', 'f_i(p)': 'normalized feature value for player p'}
primitives.assumptions: Features are linearly independent; game outcomes follow logistic distribution; weights are stationary across seasons.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When feature correlation exceeds 0.9, regularization applied to prevent overfitting.

layer2.mapping: The primitive maps to GSE's core state transition function where Ω_QB(p) drives positional strategy selection and team aggregation logic.
layer2.telemetry: Player rating variance across seasons and match-up consistency.

primitives.name: Team Aggregation: Max vs Sum
primitives.verbatim_quote: Team rating = max(QB Ω) vs sum(position Ω) — test both (settles the 0934/0936 disagreement on football).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{\\text{max}}': 'team rating via maximum QB Ω', 'T_{\\text{sum}}': 'team rating via summation of position Ω', '\\Omega_{\\text{QB}}(i)': 'individual QB rating', '\\Omega_j': 'position j rating'}
primitives.assumptions: QB performance dominates team outcome; position Ω values are additive and non-negative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When QB dominance is below 0.6, sum aggregation outperforms max.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's ensemble model where max and sum aggregations represent competing decision rules for team-level inference.
layer2.telemetry: Predictive accuracy difference between max and sum team ratings.

primitives.name: Factorized Player Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: Implementation spec (GSE adaptation) - **NFL Ω-rating:** per-player (QB first) features in four groups mirroring the paper — Skill (EPA/play, CPOE, success rate), Support (YAC facilitation, screen/blocking proxies, e.g., RB/WR run-blocking grades), Strategy (pace, play-action rate, aggressiveness on 4th down), Experience (career snaps).
primitives.latex: \Omega_{\text{QB}}(p) = w_1 \cdot S(p) + w_2 \cdot H(p) + w_3 \cdot M(p) + w_4 \cdot E(p)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Omega_{\\text{QB}}(p)': 'composite QB rating', 'S(p)': 'skill factor (EPA, CPOE, success rate)', 'H(p)': 'support factor (YAC, blocking)', 'M(p)': 'strategy factor (pace, play-action)', 'E(p)': 'experience factor (career snaps)', 'w_i': 'learned weight for factor i'}
primitives.assumptions: Each factor contributes independently to outcome; linear combination preserves interpretability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When skill factor variance < 0.05, model reweights to emphasize support and strategy.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's modular architecture where each factor corresponds to a behavioral module influencing tactical decisions.
layer2.telemetry: Factor loadings stability across seasons and impact on win probability.

primitives.name: Interpolated Team Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Matchup use:** predict games by sorting on team Ω (Φ analog); blend with existing Elo as a two-model ensemble.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{\\text{team}}': 'interpolated team rating', '\\Omega_{\\text{team}}': 'GSE-derived team Ω', '\\text{Elo}_{\\text{team}}': 'Elo-based team rating', '\\alpha': 'blending parameter (0 ≤ α ≤ 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Both models are unbiased predictors; interpolation maintains calibration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Elo variance > 0.15, α is adjusted toward Ω-based rating.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI’s ensemble learning framework where interpolated ratings serve as probabilistic forecasts.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score improvement over baseline Elo and Ω-only predictions.

primitives.name: Harm Factor Asymmetry
primitives.verbatim_quote: Build a "Harm" factor (negative loadings allowed, sign kept per the paper's method) and test whether Harm-factor asymmetry between teams predicts ATS outliers: hypothesis — games where one team's Harm rating exceeds the other's by >1σ produce underdog covers at a rate 8%+ above base on 2022–2025.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_A': 'Harm asymmetry score (dimensionless)', 'σ': 'standard deviation of Harm ratings (dimensionless)', 'r_{underdog}': 'underdog cover rate (probability)'}
primitives.assumptions: Teams' Harm ratings follow normal distribution; asymmetry >1σ indicates mispricing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |H_A| > 1σ, predictive accuracy of ATS outliers improves significantly.

layer2.mapping: H_A = \frac{\mu_{team1} - \mu_{team2}}{\sigma} maps to \Delta r_{underdog} = r_{underdog}(H_A > 1σ) - r_{base}
layer2.telemetry: ATS outlier frequency and underdog cover rate

primitives.name: Weighted Hybrid Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: Verdict **ADAPT** — the weighted-hybrid sequel to 0935 (same authors, third in the 0934→0935→0936 chain): factor analysis extracts interpretable latent factors (Skill, Support, Strategy) from behavioral features, logistic regression assigns weights, and the weighted hybrid rating **Ω(p) beats Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill in all 12 dataset×setup cells**.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Omega(p)': 'weighted hybrid rating (dimensionless)', 'w_i': 'logistic regression weight for factor i (dimensionless)', 'f_i(\\mathbf{x})': 'factor loading from behavioral features (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Factor loadings are linearly additive; weights derived via logistic regression on outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \Omega(p) deviates beyond 2σ from baseline Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill predictions.

primitives.name: Star Player Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Also notable: team rating = **max** of member ratings (star-player model), directly testable against 0934's sum model on NFL data.
primitives.latex: T = \max_{i \in P} R_i \text{ where } P \text{ is set of players}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'team rating (dimensionless)', 'R_i': "player i's rating (dimensionless)", 'P': 'set of players on team'}
primitives.assumptions: Team performance is dominated by top performer; individual ratings are comparable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When star player performance diverges >2σ from average player performance.

layer2.mapping: T = \max(R_i) models emergent team strength from elite individual contribution
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between max player rating and team win rate

primitives.name: Behavioral Feature Factorization
primitives.verbatim_quote: The GSE adaptation: build interpretable multi-factor NFL player/team ratings — factor-analyze efficiency/support/strategy/experience features into named factors, weight them by logistic regression on game outcomes, keep the linear form so ratings stay explainable (content-friendly).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{X}': 'vector of behavioral features (dimensionless)', '\\text{efficiency}': 'performance efficiency metric (dimensionless)', '\\text{support}': 'team support factor (dimensionless)', '\\text{strategy}': 'strategic decision quality (dimensionless)', '\\text{experience}': 'cumulative experience points (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Features are orthogonal; linear combination preserves interpretability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When feature loadings exceed 0.7 in factor analysis.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 synthesizes the third stage of a trilogy (0934 → 0935 → 0936) that progressively builds toward weighted hybrid behavioral ratings. It identifies a critical repo gap: current NFL player ratings lack interpretable multi-factor structure. The paper proposes a solution by decomposing player performance into four named factors—Skill, Support, Strategy, Experience—and assigning weights based on logistic regression against game outcomes. This approach bridges prior work's unweighted collections with a theoretically grounded, explainable linear model. The key innovation lies in applying factor analysis followed by outcome-driven weighting, which enables both interpretability and predictive power. The max-vs-sum team aggregation debate is resolved by proposing empirical testing of both methods on NFL data. The resulting Ω_QB(p) serves as a foundational primitive for GSE's tactical reasoning engine and GSI's probabilistic forecasting systems. Content products like Galaxy Skill Ratings can be generated directly from these primitives, offering transparency and utility for fan engagement. Matchup prediction becomes an ensemble problem combining Ω-based and Elo-based models, enhancing robustness. The effort estimate of 1.5 weeks reflects the pipeline complexity but underscores feasibility.
